The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.

2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 05.09.2022 at about 10.45 p.m. one S.Mubarak was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP- 39-EV-6995 near Reliance Petrol Bunk, near Nagamangalam on Chittoor- Bengaluru NH Road, SCCH 5 Chittoor, Palamaner Mandal, at that time, the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-25-AZ-9355 has been parked his vehicle in Kamal Basha vs Nandha Kumar B on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55528828/
2 NH road without taking any precautionary measures by not putting any parking signal light/indicator, parking barricade and also he was negligent in not being giving hand signal.

entities.text: Kamal Basha vs Nandha Kumar B

sentences.text: The said S. Mubarak dashed his motor cycle against parked lorry, due to the said impact he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Palamaner, wherein Doctor have declared that deceased was brought dead due to the accidental injuries.

Therafter post mortem was conducted in the said hospital, body was handed over to the petitioners, which they have spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremonies etc., SCCH 5 3.
At the time of accident, deceased/S. Mubarak was aged about 22 years, working as Mechanic at Kolamasanapalli, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
petitioner No.1 is father, petitioner No.2 is mother, petitioner No.3 and 4 are sisters and petitioner No.5 is brother of the deceased.

Out of the said accident, crime No.257/2022 is registered against the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-25-AZ-9355 before the Palamaner Urban Police Station for the offences punishable under Sec.304(A), 337, 279 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is owner and respondent No.2 is insurer of the said Lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

So that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent SCCH 5 No.2 / insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied the entire case of the petitioner.

There is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act and respondent No.2 denies issuance of policy of insurance in respect of lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-25-AZ-9355 and if there is any liability to pay the compensation, it is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further denied occurred of the alleged accident involving the said lorry and also denied age, occupation, income,
nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased, alleged nexus and involvment of the said offending vehicle.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
SCCH 5 ::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioners prove that, deceased Sri. Mubarak succumbed to the injuries sustained in vehicular accident alleged to have been occurred on 05.09.2022 at about 10.45 p.m. due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN- 25-AZ-9355?

2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so what is the quantum and from whom?

6. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.1/father of the deceased himself deposed his evidence as PW-1 and exhibited 9 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not adduced any oral or documentary evidence.
SCCH 5 7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1/father of the deceased has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief-examination he has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this regard he has exhibited copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2,
copy of inquest marked as Ex.P.3, copy of P.M. Report marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report marked as Ex.P.5, copy of sketch SCCH 5 marked as Ex.P.6 and copy of charge sheet marked as Ex.P.7.

9 . On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and the records those were marked i.e., FIR, complaint, inquest,
P.M.Report, IMV Report, sketch and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the accident dated 05.09.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.

Per contra, the respondent No.1 being the owner has remained absent and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-25-AZ-9355 though appeared and filed written statement, respondent No.2 not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of SCCH 5 the petitioners about death of S.Mubarak out of the accident held on 05.09.2022 at about 10.45 p.m. while he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-EV-6995 at Reliance Petrol Bunk, near Nagamangalam on Chittoor - Bengaluru NH- Road, Chittoor, Palamaner Mandal.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioners.
11. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the lorry.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.

Accordingly I have answered above Kamal Basha vs Nandha Kumar B on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55528828/
4 Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

In the said rulings of the respondent No.2, their lordship have clearly held that,
a) If the respondent Insurance Company has proved the negligency on the part of the car driver, who has died out of the accident, then tribunals may consider the quantum of contributory negligence b) In any accident i.e., when a car hit a tanker from behind, then tribunals may give findings that the tanker driver was negligent to an extent of 70% and driver of the car was negligent to an extent of 30% etc.,

But the facts and circumstances involved in the said rulings are entirely different from present set of facts, because except filing of written statement and SCCH 5 cross-examination of PW-1, respondent No.2 has not stepped into witness box nor proved the allegations as taken in the written statement.

Since in the absence of respondent evidence, merely learned counsel for R2 addressed arguments before the tribunal and filed rulings are all not sufficient to believe the case of the respondent No.2.
20.

On the other hand, on perusal of the police records and evidence of PW-1 clearly indicates to the tribunal that, the lorry i.e., the driver of the offending vehicle has parked the vehicle in National Highway without following rules i.e., by setting the indications and other instruments, those was specified under law.
So due to negligent act of the lorry driver, the alleged accident was occurred as per the arguments addressed by the petitioner counsel.
SCCH 5 21. Hence, the following calculation is made for loss of dependency.

Further petitioner No.1 ans 2 being the parents, petitioner No.3 to 5 being the sisters and brother of the deceased are entitled for Rs.20,000/- each towards filial consortium.
Further they are entitled for loss of estate of SCCH 5 Rs.15,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.

23. The details of compensation awarded is as under:
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 22,30,200-00 2. Loss of filial consortium 1,00,000-00 (Rs.20,000/- each to Petitioner No.1 to 5)
3. Loss of Estate 15,000-00 4.
Funeral Expenses 15,000-00 Total 23,60,200-00 24.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.23,60,200/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
25.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN-25-AZ-9355 has SCCH 5 issued insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 vide policy bearing No.2807003121P106651785 and for the date of accident there is a existence of policy,
it is not disputed by respondent side also and it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
However, in the written statement respondent No.2 has denied issuance of the said policy, but to disprove the same, they have not led any evidence.
So that, R2/insurer of the Lorry is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH 5 ::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.23,60,200/- (Rupees Twenty Three Lakhs Sixty Thousand Two Hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
